# Peter Robinson’s Post

![View profile for Peter Robinson]()

An excellent article by [Lucy Luckett Dip CII](https://uk.linkedin.com/in/lucy-luckett-dip-cii-540a89219?trk=public_post-text) I have seen so many 'complaints' escalated to the [#FOS](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Ffeed%2Fhashtag%2Ffos&trk=public_post-text) quite simply because [#insurance](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Ffeed%2Fhashtag%2Finsurance&trk=public_post-text) companies seem to get lost in their own dogma & protocols. Pretty much in 99% of cases the only thing that matters when you have a claim is the policyholder, so for flips sake (yes, edited) keep them fully the loop & explain what is going on. Silence is not an option. And yes, this applies equally to household name insurers as well as smaller organisations!
I was tempted to add a survey in here but then that leaves me the dilemma of what to do about insurer ABC if they are considered by those who have voted to be useless with their claims & far worse than insurers BCD, DEF or even XYZ.

![Briefing: Fewer FOS complaints begins with better claims decisions]()


![]()
![]()
![]()










Is poor claims handling the result of poor underwriting in the first place?
Surely, sloppy underwriting and poor Statement of Fact/proposal form questions introduce defects in data gathering. This is reflected in turn when claims come in. (Double negative questions is a classic example of poor data gathering.)

I just would like to see insurers making the right decision so that the FOS doesn't have to get involved! If that means investing in technical people as a second pair of eyes then that's what should be done!

How could the industry gather feedback on this without directly naming and shaming companies?
